solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Weight of stamp raised pressing single record

indicators.note: pressing means the reversed word squeezes the other pieces into its middle
in a down clue, raised means the word for stamp is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a stamp is a mark, as on a document
single is one, the Roman numeral I
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Someone asks how heavy a raised stamp is when it presses down on a single vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of mass in the metric system, so a weight in everyday speech.

clue.text: Reject overturned ballot with victory for leader

indicators.note: for leader means the letter for victory is shifted to take the lead, the front position
in a down clue, overturned means the word for ballot is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a ballot is a vote
V is the abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign

explanation.surface: An election result is thrown out when the ballot is overturned and the winner changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns VOTE into ETOV; 'for leader' then moves its V to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto a proposal is to forbid or turn it down, a synonym of reject as a verb.

clue.text: Hamper of foreign cheese mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word for the cheese is said out loud

parts.note: feta is a Greek cheese, so foreign to a British setter

explanation.surface: A picnic hamper is said to hold some imported cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is the verb. In a non-rhotic British accent the Greek cheese and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetter someone is to chain or restrain them, so to impede or hamper.

clue.text: Under pressure idiot left key

indicators.note: in a down clue, the idiot sitting under pressure means those letters are placed below the abbreviation

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
an ass is a fool or idiot
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Under pressure, some fool left the key behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport to something is the means of gaining access to it, figuratively a key to it.

clue.text: Conceive of dream, as term indicates

indicators.note: of means taken out of, so the letters are found within the run of words dream as term indicates

explanation.surface: A word in a dream is said to point to some meaning, as an analyst might suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: To mastermind a scheme is to devise and plan it, which is to conceive it.

clue.text: Ring's comprising principally rare jewels

indicators.note: comprising means the word for ring's holds the letter from rare within it

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells, and peal's stands for ring's, with the apostrophe s

indicators.note: principally means first or chiefly, so only the opening letter of rare is used

explanation.surface: A ring made up mainly of rare gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like jewellery, but it is the sound of bells, a peal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearls are gems formed in oysters, worn as jewels.

clue.text: Tricks son holding iron having no trouble?

indicators.note: holding means the tricks and the son between them clasp the symbol for iron

parts.note: wiles are cunning tricks
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A lad who plays tricks with an iron golf club gets round without any bother.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on Cockney rhyming slang: 'trouble and strife' means wife, so having no trouble is having no wife. The question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang trouble stands for a spouse, so having none means being unmarried.

clue.text: Paddled pathetically, disheartened and wet

parts.note: to paddle is to swim gently, so paddled gives swam

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart is taken out of pathetically, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone paddled feebly, felt dejected and came out soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is soggy and waterlogged, so damp or wet.

clue.text: Actor who wrestled with O. Reed stops

parts.note: the actor is Alan, written as his initial A. just as the clue shortens Oliver Reed to O. Reed
Alan Bates wrestled naked with Oliver Reed in the 1969 film Women in Love

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a famous nude wrestling scene between two actors.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue writes Oliver Reed as O. Reed, so his co-star Alan Bates is written the same way, A. Bates.
explanation.definitionFit: When a storm abates it lessens and finally ceases, so abates means stops.

clue.text: Game over following endless stick

indicators.note: following means the letter for over comes after the trimmed stick
endless means the stick loses its last letter

parts.note: a pole is a long stick
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A game ends after a player is left with a broken stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport played on horseback with mallets, so a game.

clue.text: Fugitive deserter, Yankee, keeping poles apart

indicators.note: keeping means the deserter and Yankee hold the poles inside them

parts.note: a traitor is one who deserts their side
the North and South poles are N and S, as far apart as can be
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A runaway soldier from America is held as far away as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fugitive' looks like a noun for the deserter, but it is an adjective meaning fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive pleasure is fleeting and short-lived, so passing or brief.

clue.text: Merchant is reportedly more earthy

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word said aloud gives the letters

parts.note: earthy means coarse or crude, so more earthy is grosser

explanation.surface: A trader is said to be rather coarser than others.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells food and household goods is a kind of merchant or trader.

clue.text: Mean criminal act with one displacing article

parts.note: a con is a convict, so a criminal

indicators.note: displacing means one letter is pushed out of the act and another takes its place

parts.note: a statute is an act of parliament
a is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cruel criminal act in which one person takes another's place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective (nasty), but it is the verb, as in 'that would constitute fraud'.
explanation.definitionFit: To constitute something is to amount to it or be it, as in signify or mean.

clue.text: Advance of man-eater in embrace sharing sweetheart

indicators.note: in means the man-eater goes inside the word for embrace

parts.note: to press someone to you is to embrace them

indicators.note: sweetheart is the middle letter of sweet; the two pieces share that letter, so it appears only once

parts.note: an ogre is a giant who eats people

explanation.surface: A predatory lover makes an advance, hugging a darling close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharing sweetheart': the middle letter of sweet ends the man-eater and starts the end of the embrace, so it is written only once.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress is forward movement or development, so an advance.

clue.text: Mum purchasing cool, small …

indicators.note: purchasing means taking hold of, so the word for mum holds the word for cool

parts.note: mum as in keeping mum means silent, mute
in means fashionable, so cool

explanation.surface: A mother buys something trendy and small, the sentence trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother, but it means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minute is tiny, an adjective for very small.

clue.text: Country housing centre for Galapagos tortoise?

indicators.note: housing means the country takes in the central letter, like a home

parts.note: terrain means country in the sense of land or landscape

indicators.note: centre for means the single middle letter of the island name Galapagos

explanation.surface: A country is home to the famous Galapagos giant tortoise.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a terrapin is a freshwater turtle, a relative rather than a true tortoise.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater turtle, a shelled reptile closely related to the land tortoise.

clue.text: … small containers containing ale finally? Not exactly …

definitions.text: … small containers containing ale finally? Not exactly …

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

indicators.note: containing means the cans hold the last letter of ale inside them

parts.note: tins are metal containers

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of ale is taken

explanation.surface: A sentence continued across clues, wondering whether small vessels hold ale.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: these mugs hold beer, though 'Not exactly' admits they are neither small nor ale-only.
explanation.definitionFit: Steins are large German beer mugs, drinking vessels for lager.

clue.text: Left after exercise in bandage providing relief

indicators.note: in means the exercise and left letters go inside the bandage

parts.note: a sling is a bandage supporting an arm

indicators.note: after means the letter for left comes after the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, so exercise

explanation.surface: After working out, someone left with a support bandage that eased the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' looks medical, but it is taking someone's turn at work: to spell a colleague is to relieve them.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell a worker is to take over their shift, so spelling is giving them relief.

clue.text: Save carefully, reducing irresponsibly made purchases initially

definitions.text: Save carefully, reducing irresponsibly made purchases initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the six preceding words

parts.words: Save carefully, reducing irresponsibly made purchases

explanation.surface: Advice to economise by cutting back on reckless spending.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be frugal and economise, cutting spending to the bone.

clue.text: … secret drinker seen in almost sinister clubs

indicators.note: seen in means the drinker appears inside the shortened word for sinister
almost means the word for sinister loses its last letter

parts.note: eerie means strange and sinister
a sot is a habitual drunkard
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A secret boozer spotted in rather shady nightclubs, carrying on from the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a few initiates, so obscure or secret.

clue.text: Makes a mistake apparently, suppressing large leaks

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down the letter for large inside
apparently is read as 'up-parently', so in this down clue the word for makes a mistake is read from the bottom up

parts.note: slips means makes a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone seemingly blunders while covering up big leaks of information.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog reads it as SLIPS 'up', reversed in a down clue; 'apparently' is a loose signal for that. With L added it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To spill is to let liquid run out, so spills are leaks, as a noun plural.

clue.text: Ordered and sent back, the thing conked out

indicators.note: sent back means the pronoun for the thing is reversed

parts.note: it stands for the thing
conked out means broke down, died

explanation.surface: An item was ordered and returned because it stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like bought, but it is the past tense of put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy is to put in order, so tidied means arranged neatly, ordered.

clue.text: Amorous advance?

definitions.meaning: loving and affectionate, as in a gentle loving look
a formal offer; the question mark nods to a romantic advance

explanation.surface: A romantic pass made at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means fond and loving, and as a verb or noun it means to offer, an advance of money or a proposal.

clue.text: Flash one going west helping refinement

indicators.note: going west means moving leftwards in an across clue, so the letter for one shifts one place to the left

parts.note: to flit is to dart quickly, like a flash
I is the Roman numeral one
a ration is a portion, a helping of food

explanation.surface: A camera flash is used to aid refining something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' also means dying or being lost, which hides its literal sense of moving left.
explanation.definitionFit: Filtration purifies by straining out impurities, a process of refinement.

clue.text: Record album with explosive opening!

indicators.note: opening means the explosive comes first, at the start

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
an LP is a long-playing album

explanation.surface: An album that starts with a bang, the exclamation mark added for emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark belongs to the title: Help! is the 1965 Beatles album.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles issued it in 1965 as an LP, so it is a record, sharing a title with their film.

clue.text: Clue is tenuous, time to finish!

indicators.note: to finish means the letter for time moves to the end of the word

parts.note: tenuous means thin or flimsy

explanation.surface: A setter is told a clue is weak and time is up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint is a slight suggestion or pointer, a synonym of clue.

clue.text: Excess that is, in retrospect, producing muscles

parts.note: a glut is an excess or oversupply

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the abbreviation for that is is read backwards

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Looking back, overindulgence produced muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttock muscles, the plural of gluteus, as in gluteus maximus.

clue.text: Gasp admitting heartless government's in trouble?

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the gasp takes the trimmed government inside

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for government is removed

parts.note: reign is rule, government by a monarch; the 's reads as is, a link to the definition

explanation.surface: A gasp at news that a ruthless government is in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' is an old euphemism for an unmarried woman expecting a baby; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the family way was once called being in trouble, a euphemism for expecting a baby.
